The Severance Package doesn't distinguish between categories. Everything eventually becomes cargo.

ships.name: Shard
ships.description: Crimson starter vessel. Repurposed combat drone. Mines with the utility slot, fights with the weapon slots.
ships.lore:
The Shard was never designed as a mining vessel. It was a combat drone —
autonomous, disposable, built to absorb fire while delivering ordnance.
When the Crimson Fleet needed a starter ship, their engineers did what
Crimson engineers always do: they added a mining laser to the utility
hardpoint and called it done. The weapon slots are original equipment,
untouched. The armor plating no one bothered to remove is a bonus. Crimson
pilots wouldn't have it any other way — a ship that mines and fights
simultaneously isn't a compromise, it's a statement of values.

ships.name: Shell Company
ships.description: A captured Syndicate stripped of paperwork and rebuilt as a fast pirate hauler.
ships.lore: A Syndicate moves high-value freight quickly enough to make escorts optional. After capture, pirate yards remove the ownership records, enlarge the hold, and preserve the drive. On paper the resulting company owns nothing. In practice it carries everything the raiders took.

ships.name: Shiv
ships.description: Disposable Crimson boarding craft. Gets marines to the target hull. Everything after that is their problem.
ships.lore:
Crimson quartermasters account for Shivs in the same ledgers as breaching
charges. A reinforced nose, a pilot's couch, and six crash harnesses fill
almost the entire hull. Two pilots share its only watch so that after a
capture one can shepherd a small prize home. Shiv crews paint the names of
captured ships inside the hatch, where
the next boarding party sees them while waiting for impact.

ships.name: Siege Breaker
ships.description: Crimson yield-optimized mining cruiser. Extracts more ore per cycle than anything else in the field.
ships.lore: Fleet engineers spent three design cycles trying to build a better mining laser before realizing the extraction system wasn't the bottleneck — the targeting was. The Siege Breaker's dual lasers operate on a synchronized firing pattern that hits the same fracture point from two angles, pulling thirty-five percent more usable ore from each rock than sequential extraction. The cargo hold is smaller than competing designs because the engineering committee refused to sacrifice hull integrity for storage. Crimson mining doctrine: bring home less per trip, but bring home more per rock, and make sure the ship comes home at all.

ships.name: Siege Drill
ships.description: Crimson artillery mining platform. Dual railguns keep the field clear while the laser works.
ships.lore: Fleet doctrine classifies asteroid fields as territory, and territory requires fire superiority. The Siege Drill mounts dual railguns alongside its mining laser — slow-firing electromagnetic accelerators that resolve claim disputes at range, before the other party closes to where things get complicated. The mining laser works the asteroid while the railguns discourage approach from any direction. Fleet engineers used every available CPU cycle fitting the loadout, which means the ship does exactly what it was designed for and nothing else. Nobody buys a Siege Drill for the cargo capacity.

ships.name: Silent Tide
ships.description: Voidborn stealth carrier. Moves your fleet without anyone knowing the fleet moved.
ships.lore: The Voidborn do not announce fleet movements. They consider the announcement itself a tactical failure. The Silent Tide-class carries six ships with an integrated cloaking field strong enough to mask the whole formation — hull signatures, engine wash, navigational emissions. The Collective reviewed three operations compromised not by Voidborn vessels, but by the emission trails of their escorts. Their conclusion was that the problem was having escorts at all. The Silent Tide resolves this by becoming the escort, the carrier, and the point of first contact simultaneously — a single hull where there was previously a formation, carrying inside it the formation that was never there. What is not there cannot be detected.

ships.name: Smelter
ships.description: Nebula mobile refinery. Converts raw ore to finished materials in the field.
ships.lore:
The Smelter-class eliminates the most expensive part of the mining
supply chain: hauling raw ore back to a station for processing. Onboard
smelting furnaces, chemical separators, and automated quality assurance
systems convert raw materials into market-ready commodities in the
field. The Federation calculates that a Smelter increases mining fleet
profitability by 60% by cutting transport costs and time-to-market.

ships.name: Solarian Foundation
ships.description: Solarian budget explorer. Fuel-efficient drive stretches a modest tank into real survey range.
ships.lore: The Confederacy needed survey platforms faster than the premium production line could deliver, so it designed one from common stock materials with an assembly time that undercuts everything else in the exploration class. Lower CPU means sensors run sequentially rather than in parallel; three utility bays mean the pilot selects which systems matter most. Both were acceptable compromises. Fuel range was not — the engineering team classified it non-negotiable in the first design review, then solved it through drive optimization rather than a larger tank. The result burns less fuel per jump than any other exploration hull at its speed, stretching a modest tank into working survey range. Unarmed by design: the Foundation's mandate is coverage, not engagement.

ships.name: Solipsism
ships.description: Voidborn ghost. A hull built to go everywhere unseen and do nothing but watch.
ships.lore:
The Solipsism is the perfect observer. It goes anywhere — through
blockades, past picket lines, into systems whose owners would object
strenuously if they knew it had arrived — and it is seen by nothing.
The cloaking envelope and the sensor-scattering hull together render
it absent from every instrument trained on the space it occupies. What
it brings back is everything it saw and nothing else. It carries no
weapons, because a weapon implies an intention to be noticed, and being
noticed is the only way a Solipsism dies. The Collective regards an
engagement as a failure of the design rather than a test of it. The
hull is fragile, slow to no purpose it would ever pursue, and incapable
of carrying anything worth taking; it pays a great deal to be a ghost
that does one thing. It watches, and it returns, and it tells you what
is there.

ships.name: Spit and Prayer
ships.description: Outer Rim deep-range gas harvester. Big fuel tank, afterburner, reaches clouds nobody else can.
ships.lore: An oversized fuel tank lets the Spit and Prayer reach gas clouds in dead-end systems that other harvesters can't round-trip to. The default afterburner is there for when the neighborhood gets unfriendly — Rim pilots treat it like a reserve parachute: comforting to have, expensive to use. The hold is small for a T2 harvester, and compression storage only goes so far — that's the price of an engine bay built for escape velocity. You don't send a Spit and Prayer to fill a station. You send it to find the cloud nobody else can reach, and it comes back with just enough to make the trip worth arguing about.

ships.name: Standing Order
ships.description: Sovereign Crix's flagship. A Crimson Overlord without the drone command module, sensor cluster, and Crimson siege plating that defined the original. The command suite is intact. The fleet coordination systems are intact. The weapon mounts are intact. Crix is the only pirate warlord in the sector who actually uses all of these as designed. The fury alloy and durasteel are gone — the rebuilt hull takes hits harder. This has not changed how Crix runs the operation.
ships.lore:
The Crimson Fleet uses the Overlord to coordinate battle groups because Crimson doctrine requires coordination to function — individual ships don't win engagements, formations do. Crix uses the Standing Order for the same reason, which puts him in unusual company for a pirate warlord.
The drone command module and sensor cluster couldn't be sourced. The fury alloy and siege plating are gone; the hull takes hits harder for it. The command suite is intact, running fleet-wide targeting, formation management, and coordinated fire concentration on salvage electronics — slightly less precisely and substantially more paranoidly, which Crix has found to be an improvement.
The Crix Stronghold station has a layout. This is noted because pirate stations generally don't. The Standing Order is the reason the station has one: when the flagship issues a formation order, the operation needs to be configured to receive it.

ships.name: Start Praying
ships.description: Cargo containers welded to an engine with a gun also welded to the engine. Pilot straps in outside, next to the gun. The Outer Rim said it cannot be armed. Pirates considered this a reasonable starting point.
ships.lore:
The Prayer-class documentation stated clearly: no weapon mount, no defense system, no module slot of any kind. Pirates read this as a list of things to fix. The gun is real. The power draw for it is real. Whether 14 power units running a weapon mount on a ship with 40 hull points and an exposed pilot constitutes an improvement is a philosophical question the original designers did not anticipate being asked.
500 units of cargo capacity. The gun took the other forty. The pilot still wears a spacesuit and holds on, now next to an autocannon with a jury-rigged trigger cable running to the cockpit area, which remains absent. Named for what you do when you pull the trigger and realize you've made everything worse.

ships.name: Stockade
ships.description: Crimson bastion. Carries no guns and never will — it exists to be the thing the enemy shoots while the real warships do the killing.
ships.lore: The Stockade has no weapon mounts. This is not an oversight the Fleet plans to correct. It is a slab of plating wrapped around enough reinforcement to keep that plating in one piece, and its only job is to stand where the enemy is shooting and keep standing. The doctrine writes itself: put the Stockade between the guns and the gunships, and let the enemy spend its volleys cracking armor that does not shoot back instead of killing the hulls that do. Every salvo the Stockade soaks is a salvo the warships behind it never feel, and that bargain — a dumb wall traded for a working battle line — is one the Fleet makes gladly. Crews assigned to it learn to take a particular pride in the arithmetic: the Stockade cannot win a fight, but it can decide one, simply by being the wrong thing to shoot at the right time. It will not kill you. It will make sure the ship that does kill you lives long enough to.

ships.name: Subjugator
ships.description: Crimson carrier titan. Deploys overwhelming drone swarms backed by capital-grade weapons.
ships.lore: The Subjugator deploys drone swarms large enough to darken sensors. Where the Cudgel manages a small swarm and the Executioner combines drones with boarding, the Subjugator commits fully to the carrier doctrine: five dedicated weapon mounts for self-defense, six utility slots for drone bays and drone support systems, and the cargo capacity to carry replacement drones measured in the hundreds. A fully loaded Subjugator can sustain drone operations indefinitely, manufacturing replacement units from raw materials in the cargo hold. The swarm doesn't stop until the Subjugator runs out of metal.

ships.name: Sublimation
ships.description: Voidborn refinery ship. Raw materials transform in ways metallurgists cannot replicate.
ships.lore: Named for the phase transition from solid directly to gas, the Sublimation-class refinery processes raw ore through biological catalysts that other empires cannot synthesize. Metals emerge from the refining chambers with crystal structures that should require pressures found only in stellar cores. The Collective's materials scientists describe the process as "persuading matter to remember what it could be." Yield rates are consistently above theoretical maximums, which the Collective attributes to "cooperative thermodynamics."

ships.name: Substrate
ships.description: Voidborn dimensional processor. Harvests and refines exotic matter from dimensional fractures.
ships.lore: The Substrate does not process conventional materials. It operates at the boundary between normal space and the dimensional fractures that Voidborn technology routinely exploits, extracting what the Collective calls "null matter" — a substance that exists in a superposition of states until deliberately collapsed into useful form. The extraction process requires computational resources that would power a small station, hence the enormous CPU allocation. Other empires have attempted to replicate the process. Their attempts produce either nothing or explosions. The Collective attributes both outcomes to "insufficient philosophical preparation."

ships.name: Superposition
ships.description: Voidborn drone carrier. Each drone exists in multiple tactical states until observed.
ships.lore:
The Superposition-class carries drone swarms that behave according to
principles borrowed from quantum mechanics — or possibly the other way
around. Enemy targeting systems report individual drones occupying
multiple positions simultaneously, collapsing to a single location
only at the moment of weapons impact. The Collective's published
specifications list the drone count as "contextual." Fleet intelligence
analysts have noted that the number of drones observed is always
exactly sufficient for the tactical situation, never more, never fewer.

ships.name: Survey Vessel
ships.description: Nebula expedition vessel. Deep-space exploration with all the comforts of a corner office.
ships.lore: Eighty-five jumps on a single fuel load. The Survey Vessel exists because the Federation asked a simple question: what if a wormhole dumps you on the wrong side of the galaxy? Every other explorer relies on there being a station within range. The Survey Vessel doesn't. The massive fuel reserves and expedition-grade cargo hold mean a Federation wormhole survey team can transit an unknown wormhole, catalog whatever's on the other side, fill the hold with samples and trade data, and fly home the long way if the wormhole collapses behind them. The comfortable crew quarters remain a practical decision — panic makes poor surveyors.

ships.name: Sustenance
ships.description: Solarian supertanker. Capital-scale fuel transport for fleets that operate beyond resupply.
ships.lore: The Sustenance-class brings Confederacy fuel doctrine to capital scale. Twenty-two pressurized bunkerage cells, each independently monitored, hold enough fuel to keep a six-ship convoy in deep transit for the better part of a Solarian fiscal quarter. The Bureau of Logistics designed the manifest tracking system before the engineering team had finished the hull, and the engineering team had to retrofit four additional sensor packages to satisfy reporting requirements they had not been told existed. The result is the most thoroughly documented tanker in the empire — every kilogram of fuel it carries is logged, signed, countersigned, and reconciled against three independent ledgers before it leaves the dock. Pilots note that the Sustenance is not fast, but it is consistent, a property the Confederacy considers more valuable than speed. The default damage control system reflects the Bureau's position that a tanker on fire is a regulatory matter best resolved before the regulators arrive.

ships.name: Swarm Boss
ships.description: Outer Rim light drone carrier. Launches salvaged drones at inconvenient velocities.
ships.lore:
Rim drone engineering follows a simple principle: quantity has a quality
all its own. The Swarm Boss carries a complement of drones assembled from
whatever was cheap, available, and approximately the right shape. No two
drones are identical, their firmware is a patchwork of three different
operating systems, and their coordination protocols are best described as
"enthusiastic." What they lack in precision they make up for in numbers
and the sheer bewilderment they cause.

ships.name: Syllogism
ships.description: Solarian electronic warfare frigate. Disrupts enemy systems through superior processing.
ships.lore:
The Syllogism-class proves that in modern space combat, the most dangerous
weapon is a sufficiently powerful processor running sufficiently clever
software. Solarian electronic warfare doctrine emphasizes "informational
superiority" — knowing exactly what the enemy is doing while ensuring they
know as little as possible about you. The massive CPU array supports
simultaneous jamming, spoofing, and real-time tactical analysis.

ships.name: Symposium
ships.description: Solarian command carrier. Fleet coordination through structured debate and evidence-based decision-making.
ships.lore: A symposium is a gathering where ideas are debated and refined through structured discourse. The Symposium-class embodies this ideal: eight utility slots support drone bays, electronic warfare suites, fleet communication arrays, and repair systems. The processing core array — the most powerful ever installed on a mobile platform — simultaneously manages drone swarms, fleet tactics, and an automatic minutes-taking system that records every command decision for post-engagement review. Admirals must pass a written examination on committee governance procedures before assuming command. The examination has a 40% failure rate, which the Confederacy considers an appropriate filter.

ships.name: Syndicate
ships.description: Nebula speed trader. Half a freighter's hold on a hull fast enough to outrun the need for an escort.
ships.lore: The Syndicate-class answers a question the Federation's actuaries kept circling back to: what does an escort contract actually buy? Protection, yes — but mostly it buys time, the hours a slow hull spends exposed on a contested route. The Syndicate buys those hours back another way. The hold is deliberately modest, sacrificed for a drive package and fuel reserves that let a captain pick a high-value cargo and simply be somewhere else before a raider can close the distance. The weapons are a courtesy to the optimist who tries anyway. Speed is the margin, and the margin pays for itself every time a Syndicate reaches the buy order while the convoy behind it is still negotiating with its escort.

ships.name: Tariff
ships.description: Nebula customs cruiser. The Federation's answer to every smuggler who thought scale-1 ships were the only thing watching the borders.
ships.lore: The Tariff-class is what happens when the Federation decides that border security deserves capital-class investment. Three weapon mounts discourage resistance, heavy shields absorb the occasional disagreement, and the integrated scanner suite resolves cargo contents through military-grade hull plating at ranges that make jettisoning evidence impractical. The expanded cargo bay holds confiscated goods — the Federation does not waste seized merchandise, it redistributes it through official channels after a reasonable holding period and a modest handling charge. The name is deliberate — crossing Federation space without permission costs you one way or another.

ships.name: Taxonomy
ships.description: Solarian heavy salvager. Industrial-scale debris field processing with assembly-line material sorting.
ships.lore: The Taxonomy-class processes entire debris fields with assembly-line precision — cataloguing, sorting, and storing recovered materials while the onboard laboratory identifies alloy compositions in real time. The default loadout covers the basics: a scanner for assessment, a cargo expander for volume, a pulse laser for cutting apart anything too large for the hold. What sets the Taxonomy apart is the fitting margin left over — the power grid and processing capacity accommodate substantially more equipment than the defaults consume, which means pilots refit for whatever the operation demands. Recovery reports from a Taxonomy operation have been accepted as evidence in three separate interstellar court proceedings.

ships.name: Technically Legal
ships.description: Outer Rim courier. Modified beyond manufacturer specs. Somehow still flies.
ships.lore: Every component in a Technically Legal has been modified, bypassed, or replaced with something faster. The engine governor was removed and never reinstalled. The fuel injectors are from a ship two size classes larger, feeding a 200-unit tank that covers 50 jumps at cruising speed — or 33 at full afterburner, which is Speed 6, the fastest any courier moves at T1. The safety interlocks were recalibrated to thresholds that would make a Solarian engineer file an incident report. No weapons, no shields worth mentioning, no armor to speak of. Fast, cheap, and gets you there. It passes inspection because nobody on the Rim is looking that hard. Yet.

ships.name: Tellurian
ships.description: Solarian mining capital. Deploys mining drones autonomously, processes ore on-board. Pinnacle of industrial engineering.
ships.lore: The Tellurian represents the pinnacle of Solarian industrial engineering. Its utility suite — the most extensive on any ship in the galaxy — supports autonomous mining drone deployment, real-time geological surveying, on-board ore processing, and quality assurance systems that operate without crew intervention. The ship identifies deposits, deploys extraction drones, processes the raw ore into refined materials, and stores the results in the 2,400-unit cargo bay. The entire operation runs autonomously according to algorithms refined over decades of geological research. The Confederacy considers the Tellurian its greatest industrial achievement. It is a mining operation in a hull.

ships.name: Terms and Conditions
ships.description: Outer Rim smuggler. Hidden compartments outnumber visible ones.
ships.lore: Named for what you should have read before buying one, the Terms and Conditions features more hidden compartments than a magician's stage cabinet. Hull panels conceal cavities, life support ducting has removable sections, and the engine housing contains spaces that officially don't exist. The scan-resistant lining won't fool a dedicated customs cruiser, but it handles routine sweeps well enough to keep the interesting cargo off the manifest. When stealth fails, speed doesn't — most customs patrols can't match the Terms and Conditions in a straight chase, and Rim pilots know every shortcut between here and the next jurisdiction.

ships.name: The Vault
ships.description: Crimson armored bullion hauler — a T4 freighter wrapped in dreadnought-grade plating. No guns, no gadgets, no slots to fit any: just a hold, an engine, and enough armor to crawl past a pirate base and shrug off everything it throws. Slow as a glacier; arrives every time.
ships.lore:
The Crimson Fleet does not, as a rule, build cargo ships — hauling is what you do
to the things you have already taken. The Vault is the exception they make for a
pilot rich enough to insult them with the commission, and they build it the only
way they know how: as armor with a hold bolted inside. The plating is darksteel
laid over fury-tempered plate over more darksteel, courses deep, until a boarding
crew's cutting charges run out before the hull does; raiders have been known to
knock on a Vault for the better part of a day and leave with nothing but a dented
reputation. All that mass has a price, and the price is paid in speed — the Vault
moves at a crawl, a slow gleaming brick grinding from port to port. Its owner does
not mind. When what you are moving is bullion, and the ship will arrive no matter
who objects, you can afford to be late.
ships.prestige_lock: Locked: prestige hull reserved for pilots who have earned the "Bullion Baron" achievement.

ships.name: Theorem
ships.description: Solarian heavy fighter. Balanced combat platform with superior electronics.
ships.lore: Where other empires bolt on more weapons, the Confederacy added more processing capacity. The Theorem carries the deepest fitting reserves of any heavy fighter in production — three open utility bays and enough CPU headroom for pilots to configure it for whatever the engagement demands. Escort duty, patrol interdiction, extended operations — same hull, different loadout. The engineering committee that approved the modular fitting architecture took eight months to reach consensus. The architecture then justified itself on the first deployment, in four configurations, across three theaters of operation.

ships.name: Theoria
ships.description: Solarian starter mining vessel. Certified, calibrated, warranty-covered.
ships.lore:
Every Solarian pilot's journey begins with a Theoria. Named for the ancient
Greek concept of contemplative knowledge, this vessel embodies the Confederacy's
belief that understanding precedes action. The 300-page operations manual
(mandatory reading, examination required) covers everything from optimal ore
extraction angles to emergency hull breach poetry recitation protocols.
Over-engineered by three separate review committees, the Theoria has more
diagnostic systems than most ships have systems. The extended utility bus
accommodates the Confederacy's insistence that every vessel carry redundant
sensor packages. Comes with a two-year comprehensive warranty that covers
everything except "pilot-initiated misadventure."

ships.name: Thermal Lance
ships.description: Crimson deep-range ice breaker. Fuel-efficient drive reaches distant ice fields under armor.
ships.lore: Ice fields worth harvesting at scale tend to be far from Fleet supply lines — deep frontier, contested space, places where shorter-range harvesters don't bother going. The Thermal Lance was built for that deployment. The fuel-efficient drive pushes the armored hull deep into territory that shorter-range harvesters avoid, and the dual thermal extractors work the ice while the autocannon keeps watch. The cargo hold is tight because the engineering committee prioritized fuel capacity and hull integrity over storage. Fleet ice operations run convoys for a reason — the Thermal Lance finds the field and cracks the ice. Someone else hauls it home.

ships.name: Thermodynamic End
ships.description: Voidborn capital salvager. Envelops entire capital wrecks and reduces them to sorted material streams.
ships.lore:
The Thermodynamic End is the Collective's capital salvage vessel, named
for the principle it embodies: all ordered structures tend toward
dissolution, and the Collective merely accelerates the process. Its
organic hull can envelop an entire capital wreck, breaking it down into
sorted material streams over the course of hours. The vessel carries no
weapons — the shield envelope that protects it during salvage operations
has discouraged interference often enough that the Collective stopped
installing hardpoints entirely. The recovered materials emerge at a
purity that exceeds the original manufacturing specification, a result
that Solarian metallurgists have called "thermodynamically implausible."

ships.name: Threshold
ships.description: Voidborn starter vessel. Grown, not built. Anticipates pilot intent.
ships.lore:
The Threshold is not manufactured. It is cultivated in Nexus Prime's orbital
growth bays over a period the Collective insists on calling "gestation." The
hull is a crystalline-organic composite that repairs microscopic fractures
autonomously. The shield generators draw power from sources the engineering
manual describes only as "adjacent." New pilots report that the ship
anticipates course corrections before they're input — the Collective
considers this a feature, not a concern. The cabin temperature is always
slightly wrong, regardless of thermostat settings. No Voidborn engineer
has ever acknowledged this as a defect.

ships.name: Toll
ships.description: Crimson customs enforcer. The price of crossing is inspection. The price of refusal is higher.
ships.lore:
The Toll-class was designed by a committee that included both customs
officials and weapons engineers. The weapons engineers won most of the
arguments. Heavy armor and twin autocannons make the Toll significantly
overqualified for cargo inspection — which is, from the Crimson
perspective, exactly the point. Smugglers who encounter a Toll tend to
cooperate. Smugglers who encounter two Tolls tend to surrender. The
scanning suite is military-grade, because in the Crimson Pact, all
grades are military grades.

ships.name: Tourniquet
ships.description: Crimson armored casualty shuttle built to retrieve wounded personnel from the edge of an engagement.
ships.lore:
Tourniquets wait behind the assault line with engines hot and receiving
teams strapped in. Their armored approach compartment can take a hit while
docking with a damaged ship, but the small ward is built for stabilization
and transfer rather than long recovery. Marine units trust the red-striped
shuttles because they return to the same extraction point until it is empty.

ships.name: Treasury
ships.description: Nebula luxury yacht. For captains who've earned the right to travel comfortably.
ships.lore: The Treasury-class is the Federation's rolling advertisement for the rewards of commercial success. Panoramic viewports, climate-controlled cargo bays (for "delicate acquisitions"), and a passenger suite that would be excessive in a hotel. The three defense slots protect not just the hull but the lifestyle investment within. Five utility slots accommodate everything from entertainment systems to portfolio management terminals. The Federation offers financing at preferred customer rates.

ships.name: Trebuchet
ships.description: Crimson armored wall. A cheap slab of plating the Fleet parks in front of its guns to soak the incoming fire.
ships.lore: The Trebuchet does not win battles. It survives them, which in Crimson accounting is the same thing measured from a different ledger. The hull is a slab of layered plating wrapped around almost nothing — a wall of armor with engines bolted to the back as an afterthought. Fleet doctrine parks it directly between the gunships and the enemy and tells the crew to hold position. Whatever fire would have shredded the real warships lands on the Trebuchet instead, and the Trebuchet absorbs it with the dull patience of a thing too stupid to know it is being shot. The two autocannons exist so the crew has something to do while they wait. Fleet engineers build it cheap and build it fast, because the role guarantees a short service life, and a wall that costs as much as a gunship is a wall nobody is willing to lose. The Fleet is always willing to lose a Trebuchet. That is the entire point.

ships.name: Triage
ships.description: Solarian medical frigate. Emergency response with diagnostic excellence.
ships.lore:
Confederacy rescue offices use the Triage for cases too unstable to wait
for a station berth. Its diagnostic suite compares biological telemetry,
synthetic fault states, and suit records before the airlock finishes cycling.
Separate treatment compartments let medics isolate pressure exposure or
contaminated equipment without closing the rest of the ward.

ships.name: Underwriter
ships.description: Nebula convoy guard. Shield-heavy, long-range, and built to outlast threats.
ships.lore:
The Federation calculated that purpose-built convoy guards cost 12% less
per annum than hired mercenaries, so they built one. The Underwriter's
160-unit fuel tank is the largest on any T1 combat hull — 53 jumps of
operational range before refueling, enough to shadow a trade convoy across
three systems and back. The shield-heavy defensive profile compensates for
light armor, keeping the ship functional through sustained engagements while
the cargo it's protecting reaches port. Fifty units of cargo space let pilots
recover salvage without calling for a hauler.

ships.name: Vanguard
ships.description: Crimson command ship. Leads from the front, not the rear. Fleet coordination through personal example.
ships.lore: In most navies, the command ship sits behind the battle line. In the Crimson Fleet, a commander who leads from the rear is a commander who doesn't lead for long. The Vanguard carries fleet coordination systems powerful enough to manage a full battle group while simultaneously engaging targets with its own three weapon mounts. The extra defense slots exist not to protect the commander — Crimson commanders consider that cowardice — but to keep the coordination arrays functioning under fire. A Vanguard that stops transmitting because it took a hit costs the fleet more than one captain's pride is worth.

ships.name: Venture
ships.description: Nebula trade route scout. Finds new markets and brings samples home.
ships.lore: The Venture-class was designed for the Federation's market development division: find new systems, assess their commercial potential, bring samples back for valuation. The fuel reserves support 60-jump survey runs deep into unmapped space, and the cargo hold — the largest on any exploration platform — means the scout returns with enough material for proper market analysis, not just sensor readings. The open weapon slot and defense mount acknowledge that unmapped space is not always empty, and the fitting budget lets pilots configure for the risk profile of each survey run. The operations manual opens with: "Discovery is just commerce that hasn't happened yet."

ships.name: Verglas
ships.description: Voidborn anomalous ice harvester. Phase-shifts through ice to extract materials from deep cores.
ships.lore:
The Verglas-class harvests ice through dimensional phase-shifting
at capital scale. The extraction system reaches through the surface of
ice bodies without disturbing them, pulling target materials directly
from deep cores that conventional equipment cannot access. Nine hundred
shield points protect against the dimensional stress of sustained
phase-extraction operations. The technique is unique to the Voidborn —
other empires lack the dimensional technology to reach into solid
matter without breaking it. The Collective considers this approach
both more efficient and more respectful of the ice body's structural
integrity.

ships.name: Vigil
ships.description: Voidborn patrol vessel. Shield-hardened enforcement platform that outlasts anything it encounters.
ships.lore: A vigil is a period of watchful attention — and the Collective considers enforcement to be exactly that. The Vigil-class carries layered shield generators that let it absorb sustained fire while its twin pulse lasers methodically dismantle non-compliant vessels. Voidborn patrol doctrine does not emphasize pursuit or intimidation. The Vigil was already in position before you arrived. It has been watching since before you noticed it. The integrated sensor suite confirms what the Collective already suspected, and the shields ensure the conversation lasts as long as necessary. Resistance is technically an option. The shields make it a poor one.

ships.name: Voidborn Event Horizon
ships.description: Voidborn battlecruiser. The boundary beyond which nothing escapes.
ships.lore:
The Event Horizon earns its name. Its shield array creates a zone of
absolute energy absorption around the hull — weapons fire enters but
does not exit as reflected energy. Other empires' tactical analysts
describe engaging an Event Horizon as "firing into a black hole."
The weapon complement is secondary by design: the Event Horizon does
not need to destroy its targets quickly. It needs to outlast them.
Five defense slots support the most comprehensive shield architecture
mounted on anything smaller than a capital ship. Fleet intelligence
reports suggest the power systems draw from dimensional micro-fractures,
producing sustained output that should not be possible from a reactor
this size.

ships.name: Voidborn Singularity
ships.description: Voidborn cruiser. Shield layers that shouldn't be possible. Crew reports mild temporal displacement.
ships.lore: The Singularity-class carries shield arrays that produce readings other empires' sensors classify as "errors." Four defense slots support a layered shield architecture that the Collective describes as "recursive probability reduction." Enemy weapons officers report that targeting solutions decay faster than they can be computed. Crew members occasionally experience mild deja vu, which the ship's manual lists under "features" rather than "known issues."

ships.name: War Wagon
ships.description: Crimson bulk hauler. The biggest hold below the heavy tiers, bolted to an engine that resents the work. Crawls, holds everything, defends nothing.
ships.lore: Calling the War Wagon a ship flatters it. It is a warehouse that the Fleet talked into having an engine, and the engine has regretted the conversation ever since. The hold swallows cargo on a scale that embarrasses proper haulers, and that hold is the entire ship — everything else is the minimum framework needed to keep the load from drifting off and the minimum thrust needed to move the whole resentful mass from one parking orbit to the next, slowly, with the dignity of a glacier. There is armor, technically. There are no guns, and nobody pretends the two plates will matter once someone decides the War Wagon is worth the trouble of shooting. The Fleet doesn't sortie it. The Fleet parks it: at a forward depot, behind the line, full to the bulkheads, and waits for the day the supplies are needed more than the wagon is safe. Quartermasters love it. Captains avoid it. Both are correct.

ships.name: Warbarge
ships.description: Crimson armored fleet tanker. Wars run on fuel; the Warbarge runs the fuel.
ships.lore: Wars run on fuel, and the Warbarge runs the fuel. The Crimson Pact's heaviest tanker carries enough bunkerage to sustain a strike group through a multi-system campaign without resupply, and is armored to make sure it arrives. Two autocannon batteries are not enough to repel a serious threat, but they are enough to convince the casual opportunist that there are easier targets in the system. Pact doctrine assigns Warbarges their own escort wings on the principle that the loss of a Warbarge ends the operation it serves: the math is simpler than commanders like to admit. The captain receives standing orders to ram any boarding ship that breaches the perimeter, on the grounds that a Warbarge lost in transit is worth less than the same Warbarge lost on arrival. Pact accountants have done the calculation and signed off.

ships.name: Warhammer
ships.description: Crimson bulk salvager. Dual cargo expanders, maximum haul per wreck site. Brings everything home.
ships.lore: The Crimson Fleet produces more wrecks than any other empire, and leaving salvage on the field wastes materiel. The Warhammer ships with dual cargo expanders for raw haul volume and the fitting budget left over gives pilots real choices — mount a weapon, add armor, extend the fuel range. That flexibility matters because the stock fuel tank is short. This is a local operations ship, built to strip wreck sites in Crimson space and haul everything home in one trip. The tow rating won't win any races, but when a wreck field has more loot than a lighter salvager can carry, the Warhammer earns its name. Fleet recycling doctrine: what was theirs is ours.

ships.name: Warhead
ships.description: Crimson armored hauler. What the Fleet carries in these is not your business. The armor ensures this.
ships.lore:
Isotope shipments moving under Fleet protection kept being boarded,
inspected, and — on two occasions — destroyed. The Fleet considered
all three outcomes unacceptable. The Warhead-class was the response:
two weapon mounts, warship-grade armor certified to active combat
standards, and a lead-lined cargo bay rated to Fleet ordnance
specifications, which exceed civilian equivalents by a margin other
empires are not permitted to audit. The name was assigned by the
Fleet's logistics records department without review. Commanders
transporting reactor fuel note on transit manifests that the ship
class is named Warhead, not the cargo. This distinction has
prevented three confirmed intercept responses from empires whose
scanner operators were paying close attention. It continues to
require noting.

ships.name: Warmaul
ships.description: Crimson main battle cruiser. Five weapon mounts. The backbone of any serious Crimson operation.
ships.lore: The Warmaul is where the Crimson Fleet stops pretending and starts deploying. Five weapon mounts deliver sustained broadside firepower that exceeds anything else at this scale. The armor is thick enough to wade through fighter screens without flinching. The power grid runs all five weapons without compromise. Multi-role is for ships that aren't sure what they're for. The Warmaul is a gun platform that happens to have engines. Fleet commanders consider it the minimum acceptable response to any tactical situation. Everything lighter is "reconnaissance in force."

ships.name: Warrant
ships.description: Solarian patrol cruiser built for controlled seizure, casualty transfer, and intact prizes.
ships.lore:
Confederacy marshals commissioned the Warrant after too many seizures ended
with evidence scattered through a debris field. Its boarding detail trains
for compartment control and engineering capture rather than a fast body count.
The protected transfer deck can hold a prize crew, injured personnel, or the
records that justify the operation when the cruiser returns to port.

ships.name: Warranty
ships.description: Nebula repair vessel. Keeping Federation assets in service is cheaper than replacing them.
ships.lore: The Warranty-class is the Federation's mobile maintenance platform, because every hour a damaged freighter sits idle is revenue lost. Five utility slots accommodate repair drones, hull printers, and diagnostic arrays. The generous cargo bay stores replacement parts at markup prices. The Federation offers "Warranty Extended Service Contracts" that guarantee priority repair — terms and conditions apply.

ships.name: Warranty Void
ships.description: Outer Rim explorer. Goes further than intended on less fuel than expected.
ships.lore: Named for its relationship with every manufacturer whose parts went into its construction, the Warranty Void is built for pilots who believe the map's edge is a suggestion. The fuel system extracts more range from every cell through techniques that void approximately seventeen different safety certifications, and the default afterburner lets pilots choose: burn fast at Speed 6 for short dashes, or pull the afterburner and cruise at Speed 5 for runs that reach the far side of the galaxy. No defense slots and minimal armor — the survival strategy is not getting caught, and at Speed 6, most things can't catch you. Rim explorers don't report their modifications. They report their discoveries.

ships.name: Waystation
ships.description: Nebula mobile fleet depot. Carries more ships than most stations park.
ships.lore: The Federation conducted a seventeen-system audit of inter-system transit costs and concluded that empty ships traveling back to their pilots represented the single largest preventable expense in small-fleet logistics. The Waystation-class was the solution: twelve bay slots, enough cargo for a working run, and zero weapon mounts because the credits saved on armament were better spent on bay reinforcement. A Waystation pays for itself in approximately fourteen return trips avoided. The Federation has calculated this precisely. They mention the calculation often.

ships.name: Workhorse
ships.description: A lean faction utility hull that mines, hauls, and scouts in one frame — efficient to run and competent at each, so a small crew wastes no ships.
ships.lore:
A lean operation cannot afford a dedicated hull for every task, so the Workhorse
does three. It carries a mining laser, a real hold, and a scanner, runs cheap on
fuel, and stretches a cargo bay further than its size suggests. It is not the
best miner, the best hauler, or the best scout — a specialist beats it at each —
but a specialist sits idle between jobs, and the Workhorse never does. Issued to
crews small enough that everyone aboard is expected to do a little of everything,
and large enough to have earned the right to do it well.
ships.prestige_lock: Locked: prestige hull reserved for members of a faction that has earned the "Lean Operation" achievement.

ships.name: Worship
ships.description: Outer Rim cargo hauler, usually ordered by mistake. A surprisingly effective hauler if you decline to consider the loss rate.
ships.lore:
Usually ordered because of poor handwriting, the Worship turns out to be
a surprisingly effective cargo hauler — provided you decline to consider
the loss rate. It is generally considered uninsurable, and yet it still
makes up a substantial fraction of the cargo traffic in the rougher parts
of the Rim, moving goods nobody was willing to risk a real ship on. It is
often mistaken for four Prayers welded together. This is inaccurate. It is
actually just tape.

ships.name: Yard Sale
ships.description: Outer Rim wreck tug. One job — drag dead hulls home without making you quit.
ships.lore: Stubby, slow, and built around a tow rig the size of the cockpit, the Yard Sale exists for exactly one job and is no good at anything else. Drag a dead hull or a fat wreck across three systems in anything else and you will spend the whole crawl wondering why you chose this life. Drag it in a Yard Sale and the load barely registers — the tug hauls a wreck near enough to its own speed that the trip stops being punishment and starts being just another haul. There is no clever second use here. It cannot fight, it cannot run, it cannot carry much of its own. What it can do is grab something three times its mass that nobody else wants to move and bring it home, and on the Rim that turns out to be worth a hull all by itself.

ships.name: Yield
ships.description: Nebula gas harvester. Industrial gas compression halves collected volume for maximum extraction efficiency.
ships.lore: The Federation's gas extraction division ran the numbers on fuel costs versus nebula accessibility and arrived at the Yield-class: a harvester with the longest fuel range in its class by a wide margin. Competitors harvest the easy nebulae close to trade lanes. The Yield harvests everything else. The single default harvester and open fitting give pilots room to customize for whatever the deep-range run demands. The hull won't survive a fight, but the Federation prefers routes where fights don't happen.

recipes.name: Build Universal Nav Core
recipes.description: Integrate Nebula trade ciphers and Outer Rim dark matter with circuit boards to enable unrestricted galactic navigation.

recipes.name: Build Vanadium Ejector
recipes.description: Fit an eddy-current separator that throws dense vanadium ore clear of the mining intake, leaving room for rarer co-located ore.

recipes.name: Build Void Cannon
recipes.description: Fires condensed void energy that ignores shields.

recipes.name: Build Void Capacitor
recipes.description: Weave null matter into a dimensional energy storage lattice. Glows faintly in spectra that shouldn't exist.

recipes.name: Build Void Hull Hardener
recipes.description: Builds passive plating that reduces void damage across shields, armor, and hull.

recipes.name: Build Void Lance I
recipes.description: Channels destructive void energy into a focused beam.

recipes.name: Build Void Lance II
recipes.description: Advanced void weapon that tears through any defense.

recipes.name: Build Void Laser
recipes.description: Legendary weapon that tears holes in space-time.

recipes.name: Build Void Mine Launcher
recipes.description: Deploys dimensional rift mines that bypass conventional shields entirely.

recipes.name: Build Void Reactor
recipes.description: Contain paired micro-singularities inside a nebulium-regulated void capacitor assembly for extreme shipboard power generation.

recipes.name: Build Void Shield Hardener
recipes.description: Builds a powered module that reduces void damage across shields, armor, and hull.

recipes.name: Build Void Torpedo Launcher
recipes.description: Launches torpedoes that create temporary rifts.

recipes.name: Build Voidborn Null Matrix
recipes.description: Weave null matter through a shield matrix. The result defies conventional physics.

recipes.name: Build Voidborn Phase Armor
recipes.description: Armor that partially shifts into another dimension to avoid damage.

recipes.name: Build Voidborn Phase Drive
recipes.description: Infuse an engine core with null matter for partial dimensional shifting.

recipes.name: Build Warp Core
recipes.description: Assemble a capital-grade faster-than-light propulsion core from a jump coil and stabilized exotic matter.

recipes.name: Build Warp Core Stabilizer
recipes.description: Counter-module that resists warp disruption and scrambling.

recipes.name: Build Warp Disruptor
recipes.description: Prevents target from initiating warp drive.

recipes.name: Build Warp Scrambler
recipes.description: Powerful warp disruption that also disables micro jump drives.

recipes.name: Build Water Recycler
recipes.description: Assemble a closed-loop purification system from filtration membranes and pumps.

recipes.name: Build Weapon Battery
recipes.description: Assemble a hardened multi-weapon platform with shared fire control.

recipes.name: Build Weapon Core
recipes.description: Machine tungsten and steel around a power cell to form a weapon's firing core.

recipes.name: Build Weapon Overload Capacitor
recipes.description: Temporarily boosts weapon damage.

recipes.name: Build Wiring Harness
recipes.description: Bundle copper wire into pre-routed electrical harnesses for ship systems.

recipes.name: Carapace Plating
recipes.description: Press and laminate creature carapace into reinforced hull plating. The grazers' shed exoskeleton makes surprisingly tough armor.

recipes.name: Carbon-Arc Circuit Etching
recipes.description: An arc furnace floods the etch chamber with carbon plasma, letting a single thin silicon wafer carry far more circuitry. Voracious in carbon and slow to run, but it halves the silicon each board demands — invaluable where silicon must be hauled in from distant space.

recipes.name: Carbonate Biogas Fizz
recipes.description: Make the familiar bright fruit soda with industrial carbon dioxide instead of crystallized biogas.

recipes.name: Carbonate Quantum Fizz
recipes.description: Spin quantum-moth silk through a conventionally carbonated fruit soda for the same improbable finish without crystallized biogas.

recipes.name: Carbonate Station Seltzer
recipes.description: Force purified carbon dioxide into cold purified water and can the result as dependable station seltzer.

recipes.name: Cast Alumina Ceramite
recipes.description: Sinter an alumina ceramic matrix instead of a silicate one, bonded to a heavier titanium frame. Rolled aluminum sheet and the extra alloy binder make it markedly pricier than the silicate kiln and the firing cycle is long — a route reserved for when silicon simply cannot be had at any sensible price.

recipes.name: Cast Platinum Heat Sinks
recipes.description: Cast fin arrays from platinum instead of copper-aluminum. The white metal shrugs off the corrosion and thermal fatigue that kill conventional fins, and while platinum trades below scrap the foundry undercuts the casting line — at honest platinum prices it is ruinous.

recipes.name: Cast Titanium Foam
recipes.description: Cast Titanium Foam.

recipes.name: Catalytic Polymer Synthesis
recipes.description: A platinum catalyst bed cracks organic feedstock far more completely than open-vat polymerization, drawing twice the polymer from the same synthetic compound at better than twice the pace. The catalyst fouls over a run and must be replenished, but platinum is plentiful where feedstock is not.

recipes.name: Catalyze Fuel Cells
recipes.description: A platinum catalyst bed strips the kinetic bottleneck out of fuel-cell assembly: cells seal at better than twice the pace of a conventional line on well under half the hydrogen. The bed fouls and is consumed every run — a bargain while platinum is glutted, roughly a wash at full platinum prices.

recipes.name: Caustic Polymer Synthesis
recipes.description: Use the concentrated chlorine in a chlorophage's caustic sac as feedstock for flexible polymer.

recipes.name: Cave Rimeblue Cheese
recipes.description: Culture rime milk with a needle of gloomcap mold and cellar the wheels cold until the blue veins run all the way through. Slow, sharp, and worth the wait.

recipes.name: Charge Bell-Jelly Bubbly
recipes.description: A featherlight sparkling wine aerated with bell-jelly levity bladders and noble condensate.

recipes.name: Charge Biogas Fizz
recipes.description: Crystal-melt water charged with crystallized biogas and a shot of fruit into an aggressive soda.

recipes.name: Charge Ion Sparkling Water
recipes.description: Crystal-melt water charged over a voltmanta ion nodule into a crisp electrolyte fizz.

recipes.name: Charge Plasma Cell
recipes.description: Charge Plasma Cell.

recipes.name: Chlorine Circuit Etching
recipes.description: Use chlorine compound to etch precision circuit patterns. More efficient than traditional fabrication.

recipes.name: Churn Crystal-Melt Sorbet
recipes.description: Hollow-pilgrim crystal-melt churned with fruit and set with noble condensate for a clean effervescent finish.

recipes.name: Clarify Void-Ichor Consomme
recipes.description: A crystal-clear broth laced with a thread of void ichor, glowing faint blue. Served in the dark.

recipes.name: Cobalt Ink Refining
recipes.description: Leach cobalt-squid ink into high-purity cobalt concentrate. The squid does the hard work of concentrating the metal; the refinery just separates it out.

recipes.name: Cobalt Superconductor
recipes.description: Wind high-purity cobalt concentrate into zero-resistance conductor. Cobalt's magnetic ordering makes a cleaner superconductor than the usual palladium-iridium blend — a ranch-fed alternative to mined ore.

recipes.name: Compound Armor Weld
recipes.description: Blend zinc-rich repair metal under an inert argon shield for quick field welding.

recipes.name: Compress Hydrogen Gas
recipes.description: Compress raw hydrogen into fuel-grade hydrogen. A foundational gas processing technique — practicing this will develop your gas processing skills.

recipes.name: Compress Synthetic Diamond
recipes.description: Subject carbon to extreme pressure and heat to form industrial diamonds.

recipes.name: Concentrate Ion Gas
recipes.description: Compress and magnetically focus charged gas particles into dense ion solution.

recipes.name: Concentrate Thorium
recipes.description: Extract thorium oxide from raw ore. First step in the thorium fuel cycle.

recipes.name: Concentrate Uranium
recipes.description: Chemically extract uranium oxide (yellowcake) from raw ore. First step in the enrichment process.

recipes.name: Condense Dark Matter
recipes.description: Compress volatile dark matter fragments with durasteel containment into stable energy-dense material.

recipes.name: Condense Null Matter
recipes.description: Run a riftbloom's null curd through a condenser into processed null matter. The bloom already curdled it past raw-ore density, so one unit does the work of two.

recipes.name: Condense Plasma Residue
recipes.description: Crimson weapons-range plasma residue is already a high-energy condensate, so it stabilizes into a weapon core with far less raw plasma than gas processing requires.

recipes.name: Condense Void Essence
recipes.description: Distill raw void essence into a stable condensate. Handling requires extreme caution.

recipes.name: Confit Whale Blubber
recipes.description: Grazer meat cooked down slow and sealed under rendered whale blubber, spiced and kept.

recipes.name: Construct Electrum Shield Matrix
recipes.description: Weave graphene and silicate layers around electrum conductors for balanced shield performance.

recipes.name: Construct Sensor Array
recipes.description: Build detection equipment.

recipes.name: Construct Shield Matrix
recipes.description: Weave graphene and silicate layers around gold conductors in an argon atmosphere.

recipes.name: Convert to UF6
recipes.description: React uranium concentrate with fluorine to produce uranium hexafluoride gas for centrifuge enrichment.

recipes.name: Cook Cobalt Ink Risotto
recipes.description: Sunspindle simmered black-blue with cobalt-squid ink and finished with verdigris curd.

recipes.name: Cook Gutter Flux
recipes.description: Combine chlorine compounds with raw chlorine gas under heat to produce the chemical paste that underpins most pirate pharmaceutical operations. The process is simple. The smell is not.

recipes.name: Cook Protein Rations
recipes.description: Butcher, cook, and press raw xeno-meat into shelf-stable ration blocks. A clean water source keeps the batch from spoiling.

recipes.name: Crack Hot Cells
recipes.description: Strip copper wiring for conductors, pack them around plasma gas canisters, and seal the whole thing in a casing that probably won't rupture. Probably.

recipes.name: Crack Plasma Fuel Cells
recipes.description: Quench raw plasma into a stable charge slurry and seal it in pressurized cells. Hotter chemistry than hydrogen sealing, but plasma pockets are everywhere the hydrogen barges don't go.

recipes.name: Craft Catalytic Scrubber Cartridge
recipes.description: Pack catalytic platinum sponge into a finned cartridge that burns carbon monoxide, methane, and trace volatiles out of a station's air loop. Fouls in service — life-support decks swap them out on a steady schedule.

recipes.name: Craft Deep Core Survey Scanner
recipes.description: Assemble an advanced survey scanner using the rare Deep Core Survey Lens. This scanner can detect hidden mineral deposits that standard equipment cannot.

recipes.name: Craft Fuel Cell
recipes.description: Seal liquid hydrogen in a pressurized cell for portable fuel storage.

recipes.name: Craft Military Fuel Cell
recipes.description: Maximum-density plasma fuel cell for military vessels. Cargo-efficient but costly in plasma gas.

recipes.name: Craft Premium Fuel Cell
recipes.description: High-density H2O2 fuel cell for extended-range operations. Cargo-efficient but requires both liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen.

recipes.name: Create Ceramite Plating
recipes.description: Produce heat-resistant ceramic-metal composite.

recipes.name: Create Shield Charge
recipes.description: Craft instant shield restoration cells.

recipes.name: Create Silver Superconductor
recipes.description: Forge zero-resistance conductors using silver's superior conductivity.

recipes.name: Create Superconductor
recipes.description: Forge zero-resistance conductors for shields.

recipes.name: Crystal Melt Distillation
recipes.description: Evaporate rime pilgrim water crystals under gentle heat and condense the vapour into industrial-grade coolant fluid. The pilgrim has already done the filtration work — this just finalises the thermal conditioning.

recipes.name: Crystallize Exotic Matter
recipes.description: Force raw exotic matter into a stable crystalline lattice. The process is as much art as science.

recipes.name: Crystallize Void Essence
recipes.description: Coerce void condensate into solid crystal form using focused energy crystal resonance.

recipes.name: Cultivate Bioluminescent Algae
recipes.description: Maintain zero-gravity algae cultivation tanks to produce light-emitting photosynthetic cultures.

recipes.name: Culture Beltwheel Cheese
recipes.description: Set grazer milk with an active culture, press the curd into wheels, and age them just long enough to earn a rind. The everyday melting cheese of the ranch trade.

recipes.name: Culture Bioluminescent Cells
recipes.description: Grow light-producing organisms from algae cultures for sensor arrays.

recipes.name: Culture Fermentation Vat
recipes.description: Run a continuous-feed biological culture vat to produce fermentation cultures for industrial and culinary use.

recipes.name: Culture Repair Nanites
recipes.description: Program neural gel nanobots with ceramic and silicate repair templates.

recipes.name: Culture Vatflesh Curd
recipes.description: Inoculate a culture tank and let cultured protein set into curd over a long, patient run — the slowest bed in the bay, and the closest thing to a butcher the frontier has.

recipes.name: Culture Verdigris Kefir
recipes.description: A tangy cultured drink set from veil-ray verdigris curd, faintly copper-blue and sharp.

recipes.name: Cut Focusing Crystal
recipes.description: Cleave and polish a ranch-grown focusing crystal down to a weapon-grade focused crystal. The druse already did the concentrating in its geode — the bench just finishes the facets, no raw-crystal grinding required.

recipes.name: Deposit Rhodium Coating
recipes.description: Purify and deposit rhodium inside an argon chamber to produce an optical-grade coating.

recipes.name: Distill Ember Spirit
recipes.description: Gloomshine redistilled over a cinder-sylph ember gland until it warms the throat going down.

recipes.name: Distill Frontier Rotgut
recipes.description: Nobody's quite sure what goes into it. The stills run day and night, and the results are... consistent.

recipes.name: Distill Gloomshine
recipes.description: Run gloomcap mash and clean water through a station still until it comes off clear. Nobody asks what's in the mash. The output is consistent, potent, and cheap.

recipes.name: Distill Krypton
recipes.description: Separate and purify krypton from mixed noble gas samples for optical-grade applications.

recipes.name: Distill Moonshine
recipes.description: Water ice melted and fermented with pharmaceutical cultures in jury-rigged condensation chambers. The result is technically a beverage. Technically.

recipes.name: Distill Nebula Gases
recipes.description: Separate and purify exotic gases from nebula collections.

recipes.name: Distill Void-Ichor Liqueur
recipes.description: Gloomshine cut with a measured dose of void ichor until the glass glows.

recipes.name: Drain Fuel Reserves
recipes.description: Extract residual fuel from salvaged power systems and components. Not the cleanest fuel, but it burns.

recipes.name: Draw Copper Piping
recipes.description: Draw and weld bulk copper into conduit and pressure pipe — the plumbing of any station module.

recipes.name: Draw Diamond Optical Fiber
recipes.description: Draw optical fiber from synthetic diamond cores. Diamond's superior refractive index compensates for the crude process, but the material cost is steep.

recipes.name: Draw Gold Wire
recipes.description: Extrude gold ore into fine conductive wiring for electronics.

recipes.name: Draw Platinum Wire
recipes.description: Extrude platinum ore into fine wire for relay contacts and electrodes. The metal fights the die harder than gold or silver, but the wire it yields outlives both.

recipes.name: Draw Silver Wire
recipes.description: Extrude silver ore into high-conductivity wiring for precision electronics.

recipes.name: Draw Tungsten Rod
recipes.description: Process dense tungsten ore into precision rods for weapon and armor fabrication.

recipes.name: Electrolyze Water
recipes.description: Split purified water into hydrogen and oxygen gas via electrolysis. Feeds both the hydrogen compression and oxygen liquefaction chains.

recipes.name: Ember Gland Combustion
recipes.description: Tap the banked heat of cinder-sylph ember glands into fuel cells.

recipes.name: Encode Trade Cipher
recipes.description: Refine raw trade crystals into cryptographic verification chips that authenticate exchange transactions across the galaxy.

recipes.name: Enrich Uranium (High)
recipes.description: Further enrich low-enriched uranium to above 90% U-235 for weapons-grade material.

recipes.name: Enrich Uranium (Low)
recipes.description: Centrifuge-enrich UF6 to 3-5% U-235 for civilian reactor fuel. Produces low-enriched uranium.

recipes.name: Exfoliate Graphene
recipes.description: Extract single-layer carbon sheets from ore. Extremely strong and conductive.

recipes.name: Exotic Distillate Refining
recipes.description: Process skein-ray tail glands under controlled spectrographic heat to isolate the trace exotic elements the creature concentrates from nebula gas. Each batch is small; the price is not.

recipes.name: Exotic Lattice Fusion
recipes.description: Fuse the three great nebula concentrates — phase-pearl, quantum-silk, and umbral residue — into a single exotic lattice. Only a leviathan-grade forge can hold the reaction.

recipes.name: Extract Bioactive Compounds
recipes.description: Extract bioactive compounds from pharmaceutical cultures.

recipes.name: Extract Fuel Cell
recipes.description: Drain a standard fuel cell into station reserves.

recipes.name: Extract Military Fuel Cell
recipes.description: Drain a military fuel cell into station reserves.

recipes.name: Extract Neural Compounds
recipes.description: Distill concentrated neural computing substrate from optical and crystalline components.

recipes.name: Extract Premium Fuel Cell
recipes.description: Drain a premium fuel cell into station reserves.

recipes.name: Extract Xenon
recipes.description: Purify xenon gas for ion propulsion systems.

recipes.name: Extrude Nanoplastic
recipes.description: Create nano-reinforced polymer composites.

recipes.name: Extrude Sustagel
recipes.description: Run water and nitrogen feedstock through the extruder for a long shift and fill a rack of ration tubes with grey Sustagel. Bulk, joyless, reliable.

recipes.name: Fabricate Carbon-Nanotube Circuit Boards
recipes.description: Grow carbon-nanotube transistors from methane on a ferromanganese catalyst, then deposit copper traces and durable rhodium contacts.

recipes.name: Fabricate Chemical Liner
recipes.description: Bond chlorine and fluorine compounds into a corrosion-proof tank and conduit lining.

recipes.name: Fabricate Circuit Boards
recipes.description: Manufacture electronic circuits.

recipes.name: Fabricate Enriched Uranium Rod
recipes.description: Cast low-enriched uranium into fuel rod form for small reactor applications.

recipes.name: Fabricate Fusion Fuel Rod
recipes.description: Combine refined thorium fuel rods and liquid tritium into a fusion fuel assembly.

recipes.name: Fabricate Gold Circuit Boards
recipes.description: Lay conductive traces directly onto a ceramic substrate with gold film instead of etching a silicon wafer — the first fully silicon-free fabrication route. It pours three units of gold into every batch and runs slow, so no foundry bothers while silicon is cheap; once a shortage drives the wafer price high enough, the gold line becomes the only board worth building.

recipes.name: Fabricate Hazmat Container
recipes.description: Construct a lead-lined shielded container for transporting radioactive materials.

recipes.name: Fabricate Jump Coil
recipes.description: Create hyperspace transition mechanisms.

recipes.name: Fabricate Missile Guidance Unit
recipes.description: Smart targeting system for guided munitions.

recipes.name: Fabricate Missile Warhead
recipes.description: Conventional explosive payload for missile systems.

recipes.name: Fabricate Nuclear Power Cell
recipes.description: Encapsulate enriched uranium rods in lead-shielded housings to produce miniaturized fission power cells. Dangerous to manufacture but yields exceptional quantities.

recipes.name: Fabricate Ore Hopper
recipes.description: Construct a bulk ore transport container with polymer-lined walls and integral conveyor sensors.

recipes.name: Fabricate Overclock Chip
recipes.description: Fluorine-etched microprocessor designed to temporarily overclock ship computing systems.

recipes.name: Fabricate Quantum Processor
recipes.description: Build a high-density quantum computing core from stacked processing arrays and superconducting interconnects.

recipes.name: Fabricate Rad Hardened Circuits
recipes.description: Impregnate circuit boards with radium phosphor to produce radiation-hardened electronics.

recipes.name: Fabricate Reactor Fuel Assembly
recipes.description: Assemble enriched uranium and thorium rods into a sealed fuel assembly for fission reactors.

recipes.name: Fabricate Silver Circuit Boards
recipes.description: Manufacture high-performance circuits using silver wiring instead of raw copper.

recipes.name: Fabricate Thorium Fuel Rod
recipes.description: Form processed thorium into sealed fuel rods for molten-salt reactors and breeder blankets.

recipes.name: Fabricate Weapon Housing
recipes.description: Create weapon mounting systems.

recipes.name: Facet Trade Crystal
recipes.description: Cut and polish raw trade crystals along their natural lattice into precision focusing optics — the Nebula alternative to grinding energy crystals for the same result.

recipes.name: Ferment Krypton Kvass
recipes.description: A lightly fermented sunspindle drink given an inert lift from a nullbubble krypton bladder.

recipes.name: Ferment Orchard Wine
recipes.description: Honest fruit wine fermented from honeyglobe and bottled young.

recipes.name: Ferment Organic Compounds
recipes.description: Process fermentation cultures into synthetic organic base material.

recipes.name: Ferrous Nodule Smelting
recipes.description: Smelt the dense iron nodules a slag-tortoise leaves behind into steel plate. The beast has already done the ore-sorting.

recipes.name: Field Hull Patch
recipes.description: Weld salvage metal directly over hull breaches. Ugly but effective — a salvager's specialty.

recipes.name: Fire Lithium Ceramic
recipes.description: Vitrify rolled aluminum sheet and a heavy lithium charge into a near-zero-expansion glass-ceramic tile. Lithium replaces the silica former and even improves thermal-shock tolerance, but the lithium load and slow, hot firing make each tile cost far more than the silicate kiln — worthwhile only once silicon has become the scarcer feedstock.

recipes.name: Fire Thermal Ceramic
recipes.description: Kiln aluminum and silicon into heat-resistant ceramic tiles.

recipes.name: Fluorine Nano-Etch Circuits
recipes.description: Use fluorine etchant for nanoscale circuit fabrication. Produces superior-quality boards with minimal waste.

recipes.name: Focus Energy Crystal
recipes.description: Cut and polish energy crystals for weapons.

recipes.name: Foil Scale Smelting
recipes.description: Stack and smelt mirror-skate shed scales into aluminum sheet. The scales are already refined by the creature — the furnace just rolls them flat.

recipes.name: Forge Adamantite
recipes.description: Create legendary alloy from exotic ores.

recipes.name: Forge Armor Plate
recipes.description: Layer titanium and tungsten into high-strength armor plating.

recipes.name: Forge Coronid Composite
recipes.description: Press a coronid's sol-nacre with a steel charge into solarian composite. The crab laid the sol-alloy down in lattice already, so the forge skips the three-ore melt.

recipes.name: Forge Crimson Siege Plating
recipes.description: Layer fury alloy over durasteel to create armor that laughs at incoming fire.

recipes.name: Forge Darksteel Plating
recipes.description: Process raw darksteel ore from black hole accretion disks into dense armor plating. The extreme gravitational compression of the source material makes it an exceptional vibration dampener.

recipes.name: Forge Durasteel
recipes.description: Create ultra-hardened steel alloy for military applications.

recipes.name: Forge Fury-Tempered Plating
recipes.description: Layer Crimson fury alloy with steel under extreme heat to produce armor plating that resists both kinetic and energy weapons.

recipes.name: Forge Ghost Rounds
recipes.description: Hot cells provide the energy charge, titanium ingots provide the projectile mass. The manufacturing process deliberately omits every identifying mark that imperial forensics teams look for.

recipes.name: Forge Hull Plating
recipes.description: Create reinforced armor sections.

recipes.name: Forge Nickel Steel
recipes.description: Alloy nickel into steel for a tough, corrosion-resistant plate — a heavier-nickel substitute for the tungsten-and-vanadium durasteel route.

recipes.name: Forge Platinum Plasma Injector
recipes.description: Weld injector electrodes up from drawn platinum wire rather than a refined plasma core. Platinum electrodes tolerate plasma erosion beautifully, and skipping the plasma core frees the injector line from the plasma-gas supply chain — economical whenever platinum runs cheap.

recipes.name: Forge Reinforced Bulkhead
recipes.description: Weld hull plates with alloy reinforcement into heavy structural framing.

recipes.name: Forge Scrap Armor
recipes.description: Pound salvaged hull sections into layered armor plate. Heavy, imprecise, and surprisingly effective.

recipes.name: Forge Singularity Plate
recipes.description: Beat a Gorgonia's event-horizon alloy flat over a darksteel-plating and fury-alloy backing into a finished singularity plate. Only the alloy's own impossible density holds the sandwich together — there is no other way to make it.

recipes.name: Forge Solarian Composite
recipes.description: Combine Solarian alloy ore with refined steel to produce a lightweight, high-strength composite favored in precision engineering.

recipes.name: Forge Stainless Alloy Plate
recipes.description: Alloy steel with chromium and ferromanganese, then roll it into corrosion-resistant structural plate.

recipes.name: Forge Titanium Alloy
recipes.description: Create advanced alloy from titanium and steel.

recipes.name: Forge Trade Authenticator (Pirate)
recipes.description: Finish forged cipher chips into market-ready authenticators using gutter flux chemical bonding — the same tamper-evident contact process Haven achieves with precision copper wiring, minus the precision.

recipes.name: Forge Trade Cipher (Pirate)
recipes.description: Trade crystals processed through gutter flux to replicate the cryptographic encoding applied at Haven's foundry. The result is indistinguishable from a legitimate cipher. The Nebula Collective insists their ciphers are unforgeable. Archon Mera respectfully disagrees.

recipes.name: Forge Vanadium Steel
recipes.description: Vanadium micro-alloying toughens the melt so less iron is lost to slag, stretching each batch into more usable plate. Vanadium turns up in nearly every empire's belts, so the harder steel never needs importing.

recipes.name: Forge Weapon Housings
recipes.description: Cut and weld salvaged scrap into crude weapon mounting frames. Not pretty, but the guns don't care.

recipes.name: Fry Grazer Steak Frites
recipes.description: A grazer steak with greens fried crisp in whale oil. No pretension, no mistakes.

recipes.name: Fuse Diamond Glass
recipes.description: Forge synthetic diamonds into ultra-hard transparent panels. Wasteful compared to silicon methods, but carbon is abundant where silicon is not.

recipes.name: Fuse Galactic Standard Alloy
recipes.description: Fuse Solarian composite with Crimson fury alloy and steel at extreme temperatures to create the universal shipbuilding standard.

recipes.name: Fuse Leaded Glass
recipes.description: Flood the melt with six parts lead-oxide flux so a thin silica charge fuses into a clear, dense pane. It cuts the silicon per panel from five down to two — but the bulky lead and longer melt make it a wash at normal prices, paying off only once silicon climbs above the cost of hauling all that lead.

recipes.name: Fuse Plasma Titanium
recipes.description: Drop a fluxipede's plasma sinter into a titanium melt — the animal already stabilized the flux, so a single charge of titanium ore alloys straight to titanium alloy without raw residue or extra steel.

recipes.name: Fuse Reinforced Glass
recipes.description: Melt silicon ore into reinforced glass panels for optics and viewports.

recipes.name: Fusion Pearl Processing
recipes.description: Unpack the compacted deuterium pearls of a deuteron-slug into a generous run of fuel cells.

recipes.name: Galvanic Cell Assembly
recipes.description: Pair lantern-slug charge glands with a graphene-thread current collector and seal the assembly into a power battery. The gland supplies the lithium cathode chemistry; the thread forms the carbon anode. The slug has already done the electrochemical work — this is just cell integration.

recipes.name: Generate Antimatter
recipes.description: Create antimatter in magnetic containment.

recipes.name: Gilded Chitin Smelting
recipes.description: Melt the gold-threaded shell of a glitterback crab down to assayed bullion.

recipes.name: Glaze Radiant Ribs
recipes.description: Grazer ribs lacquered in a faintly glowing cinder-urchin radiant-bile glaze. The Rim's favourite dare.

recipes.name: Graphene Thread Weaving
recipes.description: Weave inkwyrm graphene thread under a crystallized-biogas atmosphere — the biogas provides a reducing environment that prevents oxidation while the strands fuse into full graphene sheet. The wyrm grows the thread; the biogas keeps it clean.

recipes.name: Griddle Frontier Hash
recipes.description: Grazer meat, gloomcap mash, and driftkale fried together on one griddle. The 0300 dock special.

recipes.name: Griddle Rancher's Breakfast
recipes.description: Fry ray eggs in whale oil over grilled xeno-meat and gloomcap hash — the corral crew's plate before the first feed run.

recipes.name: Grill Leviathan Tail Thermidor
recipes.description: Molt Leviathan tail grilled in the shell under a spiced curd gratin — the hunter's celebration plate.

recipes.name: Grind Laser Focusing Lens
recipes.description: Grind Laser Focusing Lens.

recipes.name: Grind Precision Optic
recipes.description: Grind Solarian composite into optical lenses and mount them in glass housings for targeting and sensor systems.

recipes.name: Grow Crystalline Lattice
recipes.description: Cultivate perfect crystal structures for energy systems.

recipes.name: Grow Diamond Lattice
recipes.description: Seed crystalline growth on a synthetic diamond substrate. The diamond scaffold substitutes for silicon but requires focused crystals and compounds to achieve the same lattice geometry.

recipes.name: Grow Driftkale
recipes.description: Charge a full bank of drift-trays and grow out a crop of driftkale on recirculated water. One long cycle, one big cut.

recipes.name: Grow Gloomcap Mash
recipes.description: Seed a dark cellar bed with gloomcap and let the flush run wild on nitrogen and damp, then mash it down. It eats nitrogen like nothing else.

recipes.name: Grow Honeyglobe
recipes.description: Ripen a whole orchard cell of honeyglobe under full-spectrum lamps. Richer and slower than the field crops — sugar takes its time.

recipes.name: Grow Nebula Sensor Crystal
recipes.description: Crystallize nebula essence into a resonant sensor matrix that detects faint energy signatures.

recipes.name: Grow Neural Matrix
recipes.description: Quantum computing substrates cultivated in null-energy growth chambers. Art and engineering in equal measure.

recipes.name: Grow Quantum Dot Matrix
recipes.description: Crystallize quantum fragments with gold wiring into programmable quantum dots.

recipes.name: Grow Sunspindle
recipes.description: Flood a bank of grow-racks and bring a full bed of sunspindle to harvest under the lamps. Slow going, but one load feeds a galley for a week.

recipes.name: Hammer Scrap Rounds
